title: Path concatenation: for every type A and every x, y, z there is a function from x = y and y = z to x = z carrying refl to refl

standard_prerequisites: The identity type of a type A and its reflexivity element refl x in x = x.
The induction principle for identity types (path induction) with its conversion rule, as recapitulated in the book's own retained material.
Dependent product types and type families: a family D over the paths of A assigning a type to each triple (x, y, p).
core_obligations: Construct, by a double application of path induction, a function taking paths p in x = y and q in y = z to a path in x = z.
Name the constructed operation the concatenation (composite) of paths, written p concat q.
Verify the conversion rule refl x concat refl x equals refl x by definition.
proof_roadmap: Reorder the arguments: define a function of type product over x, y of (x = y) to product over z of (y = z) to (x = z); this equivalent type allows two successive path inductions.

First induction: let D(x, y, p) be the family product over z, q of (x = z). Its reflexivity instance D(x, x, refl x) is product over z, q of (x = z); an element of it is obtained from a second induction.
Second induction: for the family E(x, z, q) = (x = z), the element e(x) = refl x inhabits E(x, x, refl x) = (x = x); path induction yields d of the type required by the first induction step.
Apply path induction to D using d: the result is the desired concatenated path operation.
Check conversions: the conversion rules of the two applications of the induction principle give refl x concat refl x equals refl x by definition.
difficulty_reason: A nested double path induction: the proof builds one type family whose reflexivity case itself requires a second induction; mechanically routine once the reordering of arguments is in place.
